production.note: Calendar years (the car was never officially sold in the US, so the record uses the UK home market). Evo's specification panel: "On sale | 1994-1998". Other dates seen: Carscoops says "The world first met the McLaren F1 on May 28, 1992" (the unveiling; carscoops-f1-2019); autoplenum.de (a database) gives 1993-1997 (autoplenum-f1); SB Race Engineering gives "Year of Manufacture - 1992-1998" (sbrace-f1). BMW Blog: "one of just 64 cars ever made" (road cars; bmwblog-f1-2017). Evo's on-sale years are used.

body.note: Fixed-roof, mid-engined three-seat car; no open road version was sold. Not stated in so many words in the panel.

configuration.note: Panel: "Engine | V12, 6064cc, dohc per bank, 4v per cylinder, variable inlet timing" (BMW S70/2)

aspiration.note: Inferred: the panel describes a V12 with variable inlet timing and no turbocharging or supercharging.

fuel.note: Petrol V12; not stated in so many words.

drivetrain.note: Mid-engined, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description of the car, not stated in the panel.

transmission.note: autoplenum.de (a database): "Manuelles Getriebe / 6 Gänge". No other transmission was offered.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (see provisionalNote). Quote (Evo specification panel): "Max power | 627bhp @ 7500rpm". The 627 is McLaren's metric figure: BMW Blog (Gabriel Nica, 21 July 2017) "a 6.1-liter V12 engine making 627 PS" (bmwblog-f1-2017), and autoplenum.de "461 kW / 627 PS" (autoplenum-f1). 627 PS x 0.98632 = 618 hp (461 kW x 1.34102 = 618 hp). Carscoops prints "627hp" (carscoops-f1-2019), the same metric figure. See discrepancies.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: one named-author article and one database, agreeing. Quote (Carscoops, Michael Karkafiris, 23 March 2019): "a curb weight of just 2,509lbs (1,138kg)"; the same author's 29 January 2017 article prints "curb weight of 2,509lbs (1,138kg)" (carscoops-f1-2017; same outlet, so not independent). autoplenum.de (a database): "Leergewicht 1.138 kg" (autoplenum-f1). SB Race Engineering, a McLaren specialist (enthusiast source): "Curb weight 1140 kg / 2513 lbs" (sbrace-f1). 1,138 kg x 2.20462 = 2,509 lb. Single configuration (coupe, 6-speed manual). Not said whether DIN or EU. McLaren's own launch figure is reported to be a dry weight of 1,018 kg, but no McLaren page could be opened.

sources.title: Everything You Wanted To Know About McLaren's Iconic F1 In A 40-Minute Video (Michael Karkafiris, 23 March 2019)
How the McLaren F1 became the world's fastest (Michael Karkafiris, 29 January 2017)
First US Road-Legal McLaren F1 Will Be Up for Grabs at Pebble Beach (Gabriel Nica, 21 July 2017)

discrepancies.reason: Units. McLaren's rating is 627 PS (461 kW); Evo's panel prints the metric figure as 'bhp', as English-language pages often do (the Ferrari F40 record has the same case). SB Race Engineering (an enthusiast site) instead prints '467.6 kw / 627.1 bhp @ 7400 rpm', i.e. 627 mechanical hp, and gives 7,400 rpm against Evo's 7,500.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 627 PS converted at 1 PS = 0.98632 hp: 618 hp, which also equals 461 kW converted. Unresolved between 618 and 627 hp (1.5% apart, within the provisional tolerance); power is listed in the provisionalNote.

discrepancies.reason: Rounding; the two figures differ by 2 kg (0.2%).
discrepancies.resolution: Used 1,138 kg, given by both Carscoops and autoplenum.de.

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 2,509 lb (1,138 kg) rests on one named-author outlet (Carscoops, Michael Karkafiris) and autoplenum.de (a database), with SB Race Engineering (enthusiast, 1,140 kg) close behind. A second independent named-author outlet or a major magazine specification panel giving 1,138 kg would make it a normal step-2 figure; failing a curb weight, McLaren's launch-release dry weight (reported as 1,018 kg) from a page that can be opened would replace it at step 4. Power (618 hp) rests on Evo's panel read as PS, which BMW Blog and autoplenum.de support; a McLaren or BMW document stating 627 PS / 461 kW would confirm it.
